construct: Microsomal triglyceride transfer protein loads triglyceride and other lipids onto nascent apoB in enterocytes and hepatocytes. MTTP loss prevents assembly/secretion of chylomicrons and VLDL, causing extremely low apoB-containing lipoproteins, fat malabsorption, acanthocytosis, and deficiencies of fat-soluble vitamins, especially vitamin E.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Steatorrhea, acanthocytes, extremely low apoB/LDL/triglycerides, and neurologic vitamin-deficiency findings identify abetalipoproteinemia from MTTP failure.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Pancreatic lipase deficiency can cause steatorrhea and growth failure, but it does not produce absent apoB-containing lipoproteins or acanthocytosis.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The lipoprotein profile and acanthocytosis uniquely localize the defect to MTTP-dependent assembly/secretion of apoB particles.
